variants.headline: Cyclone hits the colony
variants.sub: The colony has been struck by a cyclone.
variants.body:
A cyclone has hit {colony}. The storm is established, but a particular loss or injury is not. Readers considering {target} should distinguish scrutiny of responsibility from blame for causing a natural event, and should not be asked to accept an invented damage total as part of the report.

A cyclone has hit. That is enough to command attention without a lurid scene supplied by imagination. Think about people. Think about responsibility. But do not let somebody sell a picture of ruined homes or injured neighbours as established news when the report contains no such account.

The conduct of {target} should be examined without treating the cyclone as proof of a particular response. This account records a natural event and avoids an unreported judgment of its physical consequences. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
